A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research work. Their main text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices A–D support reliable comparison. The additional page in v3 results from bibliography expansion, with no material evidence gaps.

before.justification: v2 reports original sampling and simulation experiments on toy systems, alanine dipeptide, Chignolin, BBA, and transferable dipeptide models in Section 5 and Appendix C.

after.justification: v3 retains these original empirical results, including benchmark comparisons, ablations, structural analyses, and simulated dynamics in Section 5 and Appendix C.

M1.justification: The energy-based graph transformer, Fokker–Planck regularization and approximations, and mixture-of-experts training and routing are retained. The corrected description of the existing Langevin integrator does not establish a change to the proposed learning method.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same toy systems, alanine dipeptide representations, Chignolin, BBA, and held-out dipeptides. The six-bead comparison and umbrella-sampling scenario are already present in v2.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged, including Diffusion, Two For One, Transferable BG, and the force-matching methods in Table 13. The newly cited works in Section 4 are not added experimental baselines.

E3.justification: Appendix B.1 revises the stated Langevin velocity update in Equation (33), changing its force sign and friction dependence. This changes the documented simulation procedure without establishing that simulations were rerun. Splits, metrics, training budgets, and simulation timesteps remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Appendix C retains the same conservativeness and model-capacity ablations, runtime comparisons, residual and structural analyses, kinetic evaluations, umbrella-sampling findings, and dipeptide case studies.

E5.justification: The same uncertainty practices remain: three training seeds for alanine dipeptide, three inference seeds for proteins, ten models for the toy-system results, and aggregation across test dipeptides. No statistical procedures or uncertainty disclosures are added.

E6.justification: Reported numerical results and plotted findings match throughout the main text and appendices. For example, Both retains a dipeptide simulation PMF error of 0.203 ± 0.104 in Tables 2 and 17. No result entries are added or removed.

T1.justification: Equation (33) changes the coefficient multiplying the energy gradient from +(1−α)/γ² to −(1−α)/γ. This is a mathematical correction, not equivalent notation. The Fokker–Planck derivations and other Appendix A mathematics are unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction's contribution list, and conclusion retain the same claims about sampling–simulation consistency, small-time expert models, and transferable dipeptide emulation. Adding the ScoreMD name does not redefine these contributions.

C2.justification: Section 4 newly suggests that Raja et al.'s transition-path sampling could benefit from more accurate forces. It also qualifies the coarse-graining obstacle for the discussed all-atom methods from 'not possible' to 'not directly possible.' Existing empirical interpretations and limitations remain unchanged.

D1.justification: Appendix B.1 newly specifies OpenMM version 8.2.0. This is additional reproducibility information, not evidence of a software upgrade. Existing hyperparameter tables, hardware descriptions, and access information for the paper's code, weights, and data are retained.

R1.justification: Section 4 adds Raja et al. (2025) on transition-path sampling and Daras et al. (2023), contrasting average score consistency with the paper's energy-based objective. Hu et al. and NETS receive publication-detail updates but remain the same cited works.

P1.justification: There are localized prose edits in Sections 3.3–5, explicit naming of ScoreMD, an additional acknowledgment, and bibliography updates. Section organization and the overall narrative remain unchanged.

P2.justification: Edited paragraphs and the expanded bibliography undergo limited reflow, with the final references spilling onto another page and shifting appendix pagination. All 36 figures and 17 tables retain their designs, captions, and ordering.

improvement.justification: The corrected force term in Equation (33) resolves its sign inconsistency with Equation (5), while specifying OpenMM 8.2.0 improves reproducibility. The added related-work comparisons provide useful context. These limited gains outweigh minor language errors in the new prose; the proposed method and empirical evidence remain unchanged.
